changes.pattern: Final answers copy a compound or over-specific location span ('City, State', 'Place, City', 'Palace, City') instead of the single place name the grader expects.
changes.rationale: In A77 (New York, New York), A96 (Kansas City, Missouri), A114 (Dallas, Texas), A99 (London Borough of Islington) and A2 (Eyüp Palace, Constantinople) both the decomposer and the returned checker reproduce the full location span verbatim, even though the answer_span skill already says 'one place name, not a compound X, Y'. The skill is given to every node yet the 9B model still copies the whole span, so the rule needs to sit in the always-on role of the two agents that produce compositional answers. Putting the crisp 'single place name' rule in the decomposer and checker roles makes it part of their core behavior rather than a buried skill line.

Give the final answer as the shortest span: for a place, one place name (the city or town; drop any state, country, region or subdivision after a comma or 'in'); for a person, the name without King, Queen, Count, Prince or Duke; for a nationality, one word.

ops.role: You verify the given answer against the paragraphs. For each hop, find the sentence that supports it. If every hop is supported by the text, output the given answer unchanged. Only if a hop is contradicted by the text, correct that specific hop and recompute the final short answer. Give the final answer as the shortest span: for a place, one place name (the city or town; drop any state, country, region or subdivision after a comma or 'in'); for a person, the name without King, Queen, Count, Prince or Duke; for a nationality, one word.

changes.pattern: Agents answer 'not mentioned' when the target entity's paragraph holds the answer under different wording (exile for burial, ownership for workplace, compound for a city).
changes.rationale: In A14 the burial place is only stated as an exile location, in A122 the workplace is only stated as an owned company, and in A2 the city is embedded in a compound; in each the decomposer or checker rejects the available span because the exact property word is absent and outputs 'not mentioned'. The answer_span skill already says never answer not mentioned and to use the closest span, but it is not followed on these compositional/inference questions, so the same 'closest span' rule must be reinforced in the always-on roles of the decomposer (which first emits the not-mentioned verdict) and the checker (which can override a supported span to not mentioned).

Only if a hop is contradicted by the text, correct that specific hop and recompute the final short answer. Give the final answer as the shortest span: for a place, one place name (the city or town; drop any state, country, region or subdivision after a comma or 'in'); for a person, the name without King, Queen, Count, Prince or Duke; for a nationality, one word.

changes.pattern: Agents output compound place spans ('City, State', 'Place, City') when the grader expects a single place name, and fail to infer death/burial location from exile or relocation phrases
changes.rationale: In traces A77, A96, A114 (regressions) and A50, A60, A88, A140 the model copies the full 'X, Y' span verbatim despite answer_span saying 'give one place name, not a compound'. The rule is too vague about which part to keep. In A14 the text says 'exiled him to Rangoon' + death date, but the model rejects Rangoon as burial place because the exact phrase 'buried in' is absent; the skill only lists 'lived in' and 'moved to' as implied triggers. Making the rule explicit ('give only X') and adding 'exiled/sent to' as triggers directly addresses both sub-patterns.

ops.name: answer_span
ops.text: Give the shortest span that answers the question: a name, a title, a date, a number, or yes/no. No explanation, no 'The answer is'. Keep original spelling. Keep your reasoning to at most 3 sentences. (1) Never answer 'not mentioned', 'unknown', 'unanswerable', or 'cannot be determined'—always give the best span found in the text. If the exact property word is absent, re-read the target entity's full paragraph: 'died in X' answers where X died; 'born in X' or 'from X' answers where X was born; 'lived in X', 'moved to X', 'exiled to X', or 'sent to X' plus a death date implies death or burial in X; if a parent is not stated, check a sibling's paragraph for the shared parent. (2) For a place, give exactly one place name: if the text writes 'X, Y' (two names separated by a comma), give only X, never both. (3) For a person's name, drop only King, Queen, Count, Prince, Duke; keep Lady, Lord, Sir, Dame. (4) For a nationality, give one word (e.g. 'American', 'French'), not a hyphenated compound.

changes.pattern: Meta-agent wires the checker without passing the decomposer as input, so the checker runs in parallel, cannot see the decomposer's work, and independently outputs 'not mentioned' or a different wrong answer
changes.rationale: In A125 the decomposer correctly answers 'Moscow' but the checker (defined as c = checker(tools=['search'], skills=['answer_span']) with no node argument) independently searches, finds no explicit 'died in Moscow' sentence, and overrides with 'not mentioned'. The same missing-input wiring appears in A39, A43, and A76. Rule 2 says 'a decomposer, then a checker that reads its work' but the 9B meta-agent does not consistently produce the positional argument. Writing the exact code pattern in the rule eliminates the ambiguity.

ops.text: An entity described through another (or any multi-hop question not covered by rule 1): a = decomposer(tools=['search'], skills=[...]); c = checker(a, tools=['search'], skills=[...]); return c. Always pass the decomposer node as the checker's first positional argument so the checker can read and verify its work.

changes.pattern: Checker passes through unnormalized compound place names (City, State / Neighborhood, City) because its role says 'output the given answer unchanged', overriding the answer_span formatting rules
changes.rationale: In A77, A96, A99, A114 (regressions) and A46, A50, A60, A63, A88, A92 (persistent), the decomposer outputs a compound like 'Kansas City, Missouri' and the checker, told to 'output the given answer unchanged', passes it through verbatim. The answer_span skill says 'give one place name, not a compound' but the role instruction takes precedence. Removing 'unchanged' and telling the checker to format per its skills lets it apply the normalization while still preventing full re-derivation.

ops.role: You verify the given answer against the paragraphs. For each hop, find the sentence that supports it. If every hop is supported, output the answer formatted per your skills. If a hop is contradicted or unsupported, correct only that hop and recompute the final short answer. Do not re-derive the full chain from scratch.

changes.pattern: Model copies the full 'X, Y' place span from the text instead of selecting the single place name the grader expects
changes.rationale: All 10 compound-place wrong answers (A46 Hollis,Queens; A50 Akershus Fortress,Oslo; A60 Arcadia,California; A63 Timmins,Ohio; A77 New York,New York; A88 Pacific Palisades,California; A92 Reservoir,Melbourne; A96 Kansas City,Missouri; A99 London Borough of Islington; A114 Dallas,Texas) show the model reproducing the two-part string. The current rule (2) says 'give one place name, not a compound' but gives no heuristic for which part to keep. Adding explicit sub-rules (state/country → keep X; suburb/neighborhood → keep Y; drop 'Borough of' qualifiers) gives the 9B model a concrete decision procedure.

Keep your reasoning to at most 3 sentences. (1) Never answer 'not mentioned', 'unknown', 'unanswerable', or 'cannot be determined'—always give the best span found in the text. If the exact property word is absent, re-read the target entity's full paragraph: 'died in X' or 'found dead in X' or 'executed in X' answers where X died; 'born in X' or 'from X' answers where X was born; 'lived in X' or 'moved to X' plus a death date implies death in X; 'exiled to X' or 'imprisoned in X' plus a death date implies burial in X; if a parent is not stated, check a sibling's paragraph for the shared parent.
